title.zh: 苹果切开后为什么会变色
title.en: Why Do Apple Slices Turn Brown?

content.zh: 苹果里的东西碰到空气，会和氧气发生反应，变成褐色的新物质。泡在盐水里挡住空气，苹果就不容易变色。
content.en: Things inside the apple react with oxygen in the air and turn brown. Soaking the slices in salty water keeps air away and stops the browning.

title.zh: 铁为什么会生锈
title.en: Why Does Iron Rust?

content.zh: 铁遇到空气里的氧气和水，会慢慢变成一种红褐色的新东西，就是铁锈。刷上油漆把空气和水挡在外面，铁就不容易生锈。
content.en: Iron meets oxygen and water and slowly turns into a reddish-brown substance called rust. Paint keeps air and water out, so the iron stays safe.

title.zh: 面包为什么会有小孔
title.en: Why Does Bread Have Holes?

content.zh: 面团里加了酵母菌，它吃点糖就会吐出许多小气泡。烤的时候气泡被固定住，面包里就留下了一个个小孔。
content.en: Yeast is added to the dough. It eats sugar and gives off bubbles of gas. Baking sets the bubbles in place, leaving little holes in the bread.

title.zh: 牛奶为什么会变成酸奶
title.en: How Does Milk Become Yoghurt?

content.zh: 牛奶里加进一些有益的小细菌，它们把牛奶里的糖变成酸，牛奶就变稠、变酸，成了酸奶。放进冰箱，它们就慢下来。
content.en: Helpful bacteria are added to milk. They turn the milk sugar into acid, so the milk becomes thick and sour — yoghurt. In the fridge they slow down.

title.zh: 肥皂为什么能洗掉油
title.en: Why Does Soap Wash Away Grease?

content.zh: 油和水合不来，光用水冲不掉。肥皂一头喜欢水、一头喜欢油，喜欢油的那一头抓住油，另一头被水带走，油就被冲走了。
content.en: Oil and water do not mix. Soap has one end that likes water and one that likes oil. The oily end grabs the grease and the watery end lets water wash it away.

title.zh: 蜡烛烧着烧着去哪了
title.en: Where Does a Burning Candle Go?

content.zh: 蜡烛没有消失，它受热变成气体，和空气里的氧气合在一起，变成了看不见的水蒸气和二氧化碳，飘走了。
content.en: The candle does not vanish. Heat turns the wax into a gas that joins with oxygen, becoming invisible water vapour and carbon dioxide that float away.

title.zh: 汽水里的气泡是什么
title.en: What Are the Bubbles in Soda?

content.zh: 工厂把二氧化碳气体压进汽水里，一拧开瓶盖，压力变小，气体就跑出来，变成一串串小气泡往上冒。
content.en: Carbon dioxide is pressed into the drink at the factory. When you open the bottle the pressure drops, and the gas escapes as streams of bubbles.

title.zh: 糖放进水里为什么不见了
title.en: Why Does Sugar Disappear in Water?

content.zh: 糖并没有消失，它分成一颗颗小得看不见的颗粒，钻到水分子中间去了，这叫溶解。水还是甜的，只是看不见糖了。
content.en: The sugar has not gone. It breaks into pieces too small to see and slips between the water particles. This is called dissolving. The water still tastes sweet.

title.zh: 米饭为什么要加水煮
title.en: Why Do We Cook Rice with Water?

content.zh: 干米粒又硬又干，煮的时候水钻进米粒里，把它泡得又软又松，就成了能吃的米饭。不加水，米粒会一直硬邦邦。
content.en: Dry rice is hard. While it cooks, water seeps into each grain and makes it soft and fluffy, ready to eat. Without water the grains stay hard.

title.zh: 鸡蛋煮熟为什么会变硬
title.en: Why Do Eggs Harden When Boiled?

content.zh: 生鸡蛋里是流动的液体，加热后里面的蛋白质会互相拉住手，变成固体。再怎么煮，它也不会变回液体了。
content.en: A raw egg is liquid. Heating makes the proteins inside link together and turn solid. No matter how long you cook it, it will not become liquid again.

title.zh: 薄荷糖放进可乐为什么会喷出来
title.en: Why Does Cola Erupt with Mints?

content.zh: 可乐里藏着很多二氧化碳，薄荷糖表面又粗糙，正好给气泡提供了无数个"起跑点"，气泡一下子全冒出来，就喷了。
content.en: Cola holds lots of carbon dioxide. The rough surface of a mint gives the gas countless places to form bubbles, so they all rush out at once and it erupts.

title.zh: 切洋葱为什么会流泪
title.en: Why Does Cutting Onions Make You Cry?

content.zh: 洋葱被切破时会放出一种刺鼻的气体，它碰到眼睛里的水就变成微微的酸，眼睛受不了，就赶紧流泪把它冲走。
content.en: Cutting an onion releases a sharp gas. It mixes with the water in your eyes and makes a mild acid, so your eyes water to wash it away.

title.zh: 气球放久了为什么会瘪
title.en: Why Does a Balloon Go Limp?

content.zh: 气球皮上有许多看不见的小孔，里面的空气一点点钻出去。几天后气跑得差不多了，气球就瘪了。
content.en: A balloon skin has tiny holes you cannot see. Air slips out through them little by little, and after a few days the balloon goes soft.

title.zh: 干冰为什么会冒白烟
title.en: Why Does Dry Ice Make White Smoke?

content.zh: 干冰是冻住的二氧化碳，它不化成水，直接变成气体。周围的水汽被冻成小水滴，就成了白雾。
content.en: Dry ice is frozen carbon dioxide. It turns straight into gas without melting, and the cold freezes water vapour in the air into a white fog.

title.zh: 活性炭为什么能除掉异味
title.en: Why Does Activated Charcoal Remove Smells?

content.zh: 活性炭身上全是小孔，表面积特别大。气味分子飘过来就被这些小孔牢牢抓住，空气就干净了。
content.en: Activated charcoal is full of tiny holes, giving it a huge surface. Smell molecules drifting past get caught in those holes and the air clears.

title.zh: 铜为什么会变绿
title.en: Why Does Copper Turn Green?

content.zh: 铜长期碰着空气和水，表面会慢慢长出一层绿色的铜绿。这层铜绿反而能护住里面的铜，不让它继续锈。
content.en: Copper left in air and water slowly grows a green coating called patina. The coating actually shields the metal underneath from rusting further.

title.zh: 焰火为什么有那么多颜色
title.en: Why Do Fireworks Have So Many Colours?

content.zh: 焰火里掺了不同的金属：锶出红、钡出绿、铜出蓝。一点着，各种金属就发出自己那种颜色的光。
content.en: Fireworks hold different metals: strontium glows red, barium green, copper blue. Once lit, each metal gives off its own colour of light.

title.zh: 面包放久了为什么会长霉
title.en: Why Does Bread Grow Mould?

content.zh: 空气里飘着看不见的霉菌孢子，落在面包上就安了家。又暖又湿的时候长得最快，所以面包放冰箱更久。
content.en: Invisible mould spores float in the air and settle on bread. Warm, damp places help them grow fastest, which is why bread keeps longer in the fridge.

title.zh: 为什么消毒要用 75% 的酒精
title.en: Why Is 75% Alcohol Used for Cleaning?

content.zh: 酒精太浓会在细菌表面结一层膜，反而杀不进去；兑到 75% 左右，刚好能慢慢渗进去把细菌杀死。
content.en: Pure alcohol seals a germ's surface and cannot get in. Mixed to about 75%, it soaks in slowly and kills the germ properly.

title.zh: 纸巾为什么能吸水
title.en: Why Does a Paper Towel Soak Up Water?

content.zh: 纸巾的纤维之间有很细的缝隙，水会顺着这些细缝往上爬，这叫毛细现象，所以一沾水就被吸走了。
content.en: Paper fibres leave thin gaps between them. Water climbs up these tiny channels, called capillary action, so a wipe drinks up spills at once.

title.zh: 不锈钢为什么不生锈
title.en: Why Doesn't Stainless Steel Rust?

content.zh: 钢里加了铬，表面会自动长出一层极薄的保护膜，把空气和水挡在外面。膜破了还能自己长回来。
content.en: Chromium is mixed into the steel. It forms a very thin skin that blocks air and water, and the skin can repair itself if scratched.

title.zh: 水壶里为什么会有水垢
title.en: Why Does a Kettle Get Scale Inside?

content.zh: 水里有看不见的钙和镁，烧水时它们会沉淀出来，一层层贴在壶壁上，就成了白白硬硬的水垢。
content.en: Water holds invisible calcium and magnesium. When it boils they settle out and build up layer by layer as hard white scale.

title.zh: 胶水为什么能粘住东西
title.en: Why Does Glue Stick Things Together?

content.zh: 胶水涂上去时是液体，能钻进表面的小坑里；等它变干变硬，就把两边牢牢咬在一起了。
content.en: Glue is liquid at first, so it flows into tiny dips in a surface. As it dries hard it grips both sides and holds them fast.

title.zh: 铅笔为什么能写出字
title.en: Why Can a Pencil Write?

content.zh: 铅笔芯是石墨做的，石墨一层层很滑。在纸上划过就掉下细细的粉末，留在纸的纤维缝里，字就出来了。
content.en: Pencil lead is graphite, made of slippery layers. Drag it across paper and it leaves fine flakes in the fibres, and that is your writing.

title.zh: 水为什么能灭火
title.en: Why Does Water Put Out Fire?

content.zh: 水浇上去会吸走大量的热，让温度降下来；水蒸气还能把空气隔开。没了热和氧气，火就灭了。
content.en: Water soaks up a great deal of heat and cools things down, and the steam keeps air away, so without heat and oxygen the fire goes out.

title.zh: 油锅起火为什么不能用水浇
title.en: Why Not Throw Water on a Burning Pan?

content.zh: 水比油重，一下沉到锅底就猛地变成蒸汽，把着火的油溅得到处都是。应该盖上锅盖断掉空气。
content.en: Water is heavier than oil, so it sinks, flashes into steam and throws burning oil everywhere, and you should cover the pan to cut off the air.

title.zh: 火为什么烧得起来
title.en: What Does a Fire Need?

content.zh: 火要有三样东西：可燃的东西、氧气和足够的热。缺一样就烧不起来，灭掉一样火就灭了。
content.en: Fire needs three things: fuel, oxygen and enough heat, so miss one and it will not start and remove one and it goes out.

title.zh: 为什么摸铁比摸木头凉
title.en: Why Does Metal Feel Colder Than Wood?

content.zh: 铁和木头其实一样凉，但铁传热快，一下子把你手上的热带走了，所以摸着更冷。
content.en: Metal and wood are the same temperature, but metal carries heat away from your hand far faster, so it feels colder.

title.zh: 为什么用热水泡茶更快
title.en: Why Does Hot Water Brew Tea Faster?

content.zh: 水温越高，分子动得越急，茶叶里的味道溶得就越快。冷水泡茶要等很久才出味。
content.en: The hotter the water the faster its molecules move, so the flavour leaves the leaves sooner, while cold tea takes ages to brew.

title.zh: 为什么要在雪上撒盐
title.en: Why Is Salt Put on Snow?

content.zh: 盐溶进水里会降低水的冰点，雪就不容易冻硬，化得也快，路就不那么滑了。
content.en: Salt lowers the freezing point of water, so the snow stays slushy instead of turning to hard ice and the path is less slippery.

title.zh: 冷饮杯外面为什么有水珠
title.en: Why Do Cold Glasses Get Wet Outside?

content.zh: 空气里的水蒸气碰到冰凉的杯壁，被冷得凝成小水珠挂在杯子上，跟杯子漏不漏没关系。
content.en: Water vapour in the air meets the cold glass, cools and condenses into drops on the outside, whether the cup leaks or not.

title.zh: 洗衣粉为什么能洗干净衣服
title.en: Why Does Washing Powder Clean Clothes?

content.zh: 洗衣粉里的分子一头抓住油污、一头抓住水，把油污拉进水里冲走，衣服就干净了。
content.en: Its molecules grab grease with one end and water with the other, dragging the grease into the water and rinsing it away.

title.zh: 醋为什么能除掉水垢
title.en: Why Does Vinegar Remove Limescale?

content.zh: 水垢是碱性的钙镁沉淀，醋是酸，两者一中和，硬硬的水垢就化开溶在水里了。
content.en: Scale is alkaline calcium and magnesium and vinegar is an acid, so they neutralise each other and the hard crust dissolves.

title.zh: 小苏打为什么能让馒头变大
title.en: Why Does Baking Soda Make Dough Rise?

content.zh: 小苏打遇热或遇酸会放出二氧化碳，一个个小气泡把面团撑起来，馒头就又松又软。
content.en: Baking soda gives off carbon dioxide when heated or mixed with acid, and the bubbles puff up the dough to make it light.

title.zh: 冰箱为什么能保鲜
title.en: Why Does a Fridge Keep Food Fresh?

content.zh: 低温让细菌和霉菌长得慢，食物变坏的速度就慢下来。所以它只是拖慢时间，不是永远保鲜。
content.en: Cold slows down bacteria and mould so food spoils more slowly, which means a fridge buys time rather than keeping food forever.

title.zh: 罐头为什么不容易坏
title.en: Why Does Canned Food Last So Long?

content.zh: 罐头先密封再高温杀菌，外面的细菌进不去，里面的被杀光，食物就能放很久。
content.en: Cans are sealed then heated to kill germs, so nothing can get in and nothing alive is left inside, and the food keeps for years.

title.zh: 热牛奶为什么会结一层皮
title.en: Why Does Hot Milk Form a Skin?

content.zh: 加热时牛奶表面的水蒸发，蛋白质和脂肪被留下来，干了就结成一层薄薄的奶皮。
content.en: As milk heats, water evaporates from the surface and leaves protein and fat behind, which dry into a thin skin.

title.zh: 打蛋清为什么会变成泡沫
title.en: Why Does Beating Egg White Make Foam?

content.zh: 搅打把空气打进蛋清，蛋白质张开把气泡一个个包住，越打越多，就成了白白的泡沫。
content.en: Beating folds air into the white and the proteins wrap around each bubble, so more beating makes more foam.

title.zh: 巧克力为什么在手里会化
title.en: Why Does Chocolate Melt in Your Hand?

content.zh: 巧克力的熔点比体温还低，握在手里就被捂化了。所以它要放在凉快的地方保存。
content.en: Chocolate melts below body temperature, so a warm hand is enough to melt it, which is why it is stored somewhere cool.

title.zh: 白糖加热为什么会变成焦糖
title.en: Why Does Sugar Turn into Caramel?

content.zh: 糖受热会分解并重新组合，先化成糖浆，再慢慢变成褐色，还散发出特别的焦香。
content.en: Heat breaks sugar apart and rebuilds it, first melting to syrup and then browning slowly, giving off that caramel smell.

title.zh: 面包烤过为什么那么香
title.en: Why Does Toasted Bread Smell So Good?

content.zh: 面包里的糖和蛋白质在加热时发生变化，生成几百种香味物质，这就是烤面包的香气。
content.en: Sugars and proteins in the bread react when heated, making hundreds of smelly compounds, and that is the toast smell.

title.zh: 金属为什么能导电
title.en: Why Do Metals Conduct Electricity?

content.zh: 金属里有许多能自由跑动的电子，一加上电压它们就一起往一个方向跑，电流就通了。
content.en: Metals hold electrons that are free to move, and a voltage sends them all the same way, which is an electric current.

title.zh: 塑料为什么不导电
title.en: Why Doesn't Plastic Conduct Electricity?

content.zh: 塑料里的电子被牢牢绑住，跑不动，电流过不去。所以它成了电线外面那层护皮。
content.en: In plastic the electrons are tightly held and cannot move, so no current flows, which is why it makes a safe wire covering.

title.zh: 钻石和铅笔芯为什么是同一种东西
title.en: Why Are Diamond and Pencil Lead the Same Stuff?

content.zh: 两者都是碳，只是原子排列不同：钻石排得又紧又硬又亮，石墨排得松软又滑。
content.en: Both are carbon and only the arrangement differs, with diamond packed tight and hard while graphite is loose and slippery.

title.zh: 空气是由什么组成的
title.en: What Is Air Made Of?

content.zh: 空气里大约 78% 是氮气、21% 是氧气，剩下的是二氧化碳、水蒸气和稀有气体。
content.en: Air is roughly 78 percent nitrogen and 21 percent oxygen, with carbon dioxide, water vapour and rare gases making up the rest.

title.zh: 氧气为什么能让火烧得更旺
title.en: Why Does Oxygen Make Fire Fiercer?

content.zh: 燃烧就是东西和氧气结合。氧气越多，结合得越快越猛，火自然烧得更旺。
content.en: Burning is a substance joining with oxygen, so more oxygen means faster, fiercer burning and the flame grows.

title.zh: 二氧化碳为什么能灭火
title.en: Why Does Carbon Dioxide Put Out Fires?

content.zh: 二氧化碳比空气重，会沉下来把火盖住，断了氧气，火就灭了，还不会留下水渍。
content.en: Carbon dioxide is heavier than air, so it sinks over the flame and cuts off the oxygen, and the fire dies with nothing getting wet.

title.zh: 漂白水为什么能把衣服漂白
title.en: Why Does Bleach Whiten Clothes?

content.zh: 漂白剂能把让污渍显色的分子结构破坏掉，颜色就褪了。用多了也会把布料一起伤到。
content.en: Bleach breaks up the molecules that give a stain its colour so the colour fades, though too much of it damages the fabric too.

title.zh: 防晒霜为什么能挡住太阳
title.en: How Does Sunscreen Protect You?

content.zh: 防晒霜里的成分要么把紫外线反射掉，要么把它吸收掉，不让它伤到皮肤。
content.en: Sunscreen either reflects ultraviolet light or absorbs it, so it never reaches and damages your skin.

title.zh: 香水为什么越放越少
title.en: Why Does Perfume Slowly Disappear?

content.zh: 香水里的香料很容易挥发，分子不断飘到空气里。瓶子没盖好，几年就淡得闻不到了。
content.en: The scent chemicals evaporate easily and drift into the air all the time, so a bottle left open fades within years.

title.zh: 生石灰遇水为什么会发烫
title.en: Why Does Quicklime Get Hot in Water?

content.zh: 生石灰和水反应生成熟石灰，同时放出大量的热，摸上去甚至能把水烧开。
content.en: Quicklime reacts with water to make slaked lime and gives out a lot of heat, enough to boil the water it sits in.

title.zh: 电池为什么能供电
title.en: Why Can a Battery Give Electricity?

content.zh: 电池里装着两种化学物质，它们发生反应时会把电子推出来，电子流过电线就成了电。
content.en: A battery holds two chemicals that react and push electrons out, and those electrons flowing along a wire are the current.

title.zh: 蜡烛的火苗为什么是黄色的
title.en: Why Is a Candle Flame Yellow?

content.zh: 火焰里的小碳粒被烧得又热又亮，发出黄光。氧气足时它们烧得干净，火苗就偏蓝。
content.en: Tiny soot particles in the flame get hot and glow yellow, and with plenty of oxygen they burn away so the flame turns blue.

title.zh: 硬水和软水有什么不一样
title.en: What Is the Difference Between Hard and Soft Water?

content.zh: 含钙镁多的就是硬水，容易结水垢、肥皂也不爱起泡；含得少的是软水，洗东西更省皂。
content.en: Water rich in calcium and magnesium is hard, leaving scale and making soap lather poorly, while soft water has little of either.

title.zh: 柠檬汁为什么能去掉鱼腥味
title.en: Why Does Lemon Juice Remove Fishy Smells?

content.zh: 鱼腥味来自碱性的胺类物质，柠檬里的酸跟它中和，腥味就淡了，还留下清香。
content.en: Fishy smells come from alkaline amines and the acid in lemon neutralises them, leaving a fresh scent instead.

title.zh: 饭菜为什么会馊
title.en: Why Does Leftover Food Go Off?

content.zh: 空气里的细菌落到饭菜上大量繁殖，把养分分解成酸和臭味物质。天热时它们长得最快。
content.en: Bacteria from the air land on food and multiply, breaking it down into sour, smelly compounds, and warm weather speeds them up.

title.zh: 橡胶为什么有弹性
title.en: Why Is Rubber Stretchy?

content.zh: 橡胶分子像一团乱绕的长链，一拉就伸直、一松就缩回原样，所以能弹回来。
content.en: Rubber is made of long tangled chains that straighten when pulled and coil back when let go, so it springs back.

title.zh: 玻璃为什么是透明的
title.en: Why Is Glass Transparent?

content.zh: 玻璃里的电子不容易吸收可见光，光直接穿了过去，所以我们能透过它看到对面。
content.en: The electrons in glass do not absorb visible light, so light passes straight through and you can see the other side.

title.zh: 金属为什么会发亮
title.en: Why Do Metals Shine?

content.zh: 金属表面有许多自由电子，能把照上去的光几乎全部反射回来，看着就亮闪闪的。
content.en: Free electrons at a metal's surface reflect almost all the light that hits it, which is why metals look shiny.

title.zh: 塑料为什么几百年都不烂
title.en: Why Doesn't Plastic Rot for Centuries?

content.zh: 塑料的分子链又长又结实，细菌没有能咬开它们的酶。所以它要几百年才能慢慢分解。
content.en: Plastic molecules are long and tough and bacteria have no enzyme to break them, so it takes centuries to fall apart.
